# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if any code path returns an error the
model does not sanction.

## http-headers

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HH-01` | `build` | An MCP-Protocol-Version header that is absent, repeated, malformed or different from the protocolVersion in _meta is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400. |
| `HH-02` | `build` | An Mcp-Method header that differs from the body method is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400. |
| `HH-03` | `build` | A request without an Mcp-Method header, or with a repeated, empty or malformed one, is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400. |
| `HH-04` | `build` | An Mcp-Name header that differs from params.name, params.uri for resources/read, is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400; a Base64-wrapped Mcp-Name is decoded before the comparison. |
| `HH-05` | `build` | Optional whitespace around a header value is not part of the value, so a padded Mcp-Name equal to params.name is accepted. |
| `HH-06` | `build` | Mcp-Name is required on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get, and a request without it is refused as headerMismatch before the method is routed; it is not required on other methods. |
| `HH-07` | `build` | Header names are compared without regard to case. |
| `HH-08` | `build` | Header values are compared exactly, so a method value that differs from the body method only in case is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400. |
| `HH-09` | `build` | A parameter header wrapped as =?base64?...?= is decoded before it is compared with the body value, and an unwrapped value is compared as it is. |
| `HH-10` | `build` | A Base64 parameter header with missing padding, characters outside the alphabet, padding inside the text or non-canonical trailing bits is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400. |
| `HH-11` | `build` | A value that only resembles the sentinel, with a missing closing mark, a missing opening mark or the wrong case, is a literal and is compared as written. |
| `HH-12` | `build` | A parameter header that is omitted while the body carries a value, that differs from it, or that is repeated or malformed is refused as headerMismatch (-32020) with HTTP status 400; when the body value is null or absent the header is not expected; an unrecognized parameter header is ignored. |
| `HH-13` | `build` | An integer parameter header is compared numerically with the body number within the safe integer range, and a boolean parameter header is exactly true or false. |

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `LC-03` | `build` | A request whose _meta omits clientInfo is served, because the client identity is optional. |
| `LC-04` | `build` | A request for a protocol version the server does not support is refused as unsupportedProtocolVersion (-32022) with HTTP status 400, listing the supported versions in data.supported and echoing the requested version in data.requested. |
| `LC-05` | `build` | Every successful result carries resultType and the server identity under _meta io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, and is sent with HTTP status 200. |
| `LC-06` | `build` | A method the server does not offer, whether removed from the protocol, unknown, or gated on a capability the server did not declare, is refused as methodNotFound (-32601) with HTTP status 404. |
| `LC-07` | `build` | A request that needs a client capability the client did not declare is refused as missingRequiredClientCapability (-32021) with HTTP status 400, naming the requirement as a ClientCapabilities object in data.requiredCapabilities. |
| `LC-08` | `build` | Every refusal is a JSON-RPC error response that echoes the request id, or has no id member when the text is not JSON (-32700) or is not a single request with a readable id (-32600: batch, notification, response, bad id, bad version, missing or non-text method, non-object params); the member is never null, and a kernel-checked theorem states that an error built without an id has none. |
| `LC-09` | `build` | The core decides the HTTP status of every outcome: 200 for a result, 400 for -32700, -32600, -32602, -32020, -32021 and -32022, 404 for -32601, 405 with Allow POST for any request method other than POST, and 500 for a frame it cannot read; a kernel-checked theorem states that the status follows the code. |
| `LC-10` | `build` | The checks run in a fixed order, _meta then headers then protocol version then route and capability then params, and an earlier fault is reported whatever later faults the same request carries. |
| `LC-11` | `build` | The response depends only on the request method, the header fields the core reads and the body; the request target and every other header field leave it unchanged. |
| `LC-12` | `build` | The vectors are taken from the pinned conformance suite, whose requirements file for 2026-07-28 has the recorded checksum, and the vendored files match the recorded manifest checksum; the vectors are falsifying evidence and not the verdict of the suite run. |
| `LC-13` | `build` | The oracle executes the package generated from the LexLean lifecycle root, whose recorded digest and provenance match the committed files. |
| `LC-14` | `build` | Every request that the pinned scenarios send is a vector or is listed as a probe that is not run with its owning issue, and every check identifier the scenarios emit is covered, listed as not run, or listed as unreached by the fixture. |
| `LC-15` | `build` | The response bodies the root writes in the vector and boundary tests validate against the MCP 2026-07-28 JSON Schema at the pinned specification commit, whose vendored file has the recorded checksum: as a JSON-RPC response, as the typed result response of the request's method, and as the typed error of its code. A validator is falsifying evidence and not the oracle for the protocol, which MCP#6 binds. |
| `LC-16` | `build` | The exported root needs no stack that grows with its input: its recorded effects do not include recursion, no function of the generated package is on a call cycle, and frames with two hundred thousand header fields, four hundred thousand arguments, a quarter-mebibyte string, the deepest admitted JSON nesting and a long Base64 parameter header complete on a 2 MiB stack. |

| `TK-01` | `build` | The server declares the extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks under capabilities.extensions of its server/discover result, with the empty object that means support without settings, and declares no capabilities.tasks member; the declaration is the server's and does not depend on what the client declared. |

| `TK-03` | `build` | Whether a tools/call becomes a task is the server's decision and no request member asks for it: a tool that supports tasks answers a client that declared the extension with a CreateTaskResult and any other client with the result it would have returned at once; a tool that does not support tasks never answers a task, whatever a legacy task member of the request says; the arguments are validated and the rate limit applies before a task is created. |
| `TK-04` | `build` | A tools/call of a tool that can only be a task, from a client that did not declare the extension, is refused as missingRequiredClientCapability (-32021, HTTP 400) with data.requiredCapabilities.extensions naming the extension, and creates no task. |
| `TK-05` | `build` | A created task is answered as a flat CreateTaskResult: resultType task and the task's taskId, status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt and ttlMs at the top level, with no nested task member, no result, error, inputRequests or requestState, and no notification; the identifier and the instants are the host's, and a tasks/get for the identifier resolves as soon as the result is returned, because the task is in the table the response returns. |
| `TK-06` | `build` | ttlMs and pollIntervalMs are integers in milliseconds (ttlMs null when unlimited) and the legacy ttl and pollInterval members are not written; a task is kept for its ttlMs and is dropped from the table, and so answered as unknown, only once that has elapsed; the inlined result carries no related-task _meta. |
| `TK-07` | `build` | tasks/get answers the DetailedTask of the instant it is asked: working without a result, input_required with inputRequests, completed with the tool's result inlined (a tool error is completed with isError true), failed with the JSON-RPC error and no result, or cancelled; resultType is complete and no requestState is written; a working task whose work has finished by the host's clock is answered as finished. |
| `TK-08` | `build` | tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel for a task the table does not hold are refused as invalidParams (-32602, HTTP 400), and tasks/result and tasks/list, which the extension removed, are not offered: methodNotFound (-32601, HTTP 404). |
| `TK-09` | `build` | tasks/cancel is acknowledged with an empty result whose resultType is complete; a working or waiting task becomes cancelled; a task that is already terminal, or that finished by the host's clock before the cancel arrived, is acknowledged and stays as it was. |
| `TK-10` | `build` | A task that waits for input is answered input_required with inputRequests keyed by identifiers that are unique over the task; tasks/update with inputResponses is acknowledged with an empty result and removes the keys it answers; answers to keys that are not outstanding are ignored; the task stays input_required while any key remains and resumes when none does; a task that is not waiting for input is not changed by an update. |

The pinned scenario tasks-status-notifications sends no request, so no vector stands for this row. |
| `TK-13` | `build` | A tool that asks for input before it becomes a task answers its first round with an input_required result that carries inputRequests and no taskId, and its last round with a CreateTaskResult that carries no requestState or inputRequests, whose task finishes with a result that reflects the answer given; the last round is refused to a client that did not declare the extension. |
| `TK-14` | `build` | The task lifecycle is stated in kernel-checked theorems: a task in a terminal state is not changed by settling, answering or cancelling; an update changes a task only while it is input_required; cancelling a working or waiting task yields a cancelled task; only a completed task carries a result; every step keeps the task's identifier and creation instant; a task is expired only once its ttl has elapsed. |
| `TK-15` | `build` | The core keeps no task state: the host supplies a clock, the identifier of a task the request may create and the task table with each request, and stores the table the response returns; a table that cannot be read, a host that supplies no identifier and a frame whose host section is cut or is not text are server errors (-32603 or the fixed internal body, HTTP 500) that leave the table as it was; the table is returned only when a task was created or touched. |
| `TK-16` | `build` | The ten tasks scenarios at the pinned suite commit and the pinned ext-tasks commit are accounted for: every request they send is a step of vectors/tasks.json with its file and line, every check id they emit is covered or listed with its reason, the vendored files match the checksums the authorities record, and the requirements file runs the scenarios as extension scenarios that are not scored. |

## transport

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SH-01` | `build` | A request that accepts text/event-stream and is answered with HTTP status 200 and progress notifications is answered as an event stream with Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering no; the body is the notifications in the order the tool produced them and then the result, each message one event of a single data line holding the compact JSON-RPC message and ending in a blank line, with no id, event or retry field because resumption is not supported, so that a client following the WHATWG event stream format reads the messages in order with the result last; a kernel-checked theorem states the framing. |
| `SH-02` | `build` | An answer that is not an event stream is the single JSON object with Content-Type application/json: when the request does not accept text/event-stream (no Accept field, a media range other than the event stream itself, or a weight of zero), when the answer carries no notification, and for every status other than 200; a client that does not accept the stream receives the result alone, without the progress notifications; kernel-checked theorems state the cases of the Accept field. |
| `SH-03` | `build` | Every POST is its own exchange and its own response stream: the answer to a request is a function of its frame alone, so the concurrent POSTs of server-sse-multiple-streams are independent, each stream carries only its own request id and progress token, and the core keeps nothing between them; one stream per connection and the closing of a stream as cancellation belong to the host adapter (PrismPM#216). |
| `SH-04` | `build` | A request whose Origin is present and names a host outside the allow-list (the loopback names localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] with any port, and the names the host adds to the frame) is refused as forbiddenOrigin with HTTP status 403 and a JSON-RPC error with code -32000 and no id member, before the method, the body or the provider is read; a request whose Origin and Host both name an allowed host is served as before; a kernel-checked theorem states that a refused request is answered by the refusal alone. |
| `SH-05` | `build` | A request whose Host is present and names a host outside the allow-list is refused as forbiddenHost with HTTP status 403 and the same body shape; the Origin is judged before the Host; a request with no Origin, or with no Host, is not refused for its absence, because a browser sends both on a rebinding request and a client that is not a browser sends neither. |
| `SH-06` | `build` | The streaming probes of server-stateless that issue 7 left to this issue: server/discover advertises no listChanged and no subscribe capability and subscriptions/listen is answered as methodNotFound (-32601, HTTP status 404), which the scenario reads as a feature that is absent, so the probes at lines 1037 and 1144 are vectors and those at 1209 and 1279 are not reached; the probes at lines 887 and 947 need diagnostic tools the fixture does not list and are listed as not run. |
| `SH-07` | `build` | An Origin or Host the core cannot judge is refused like a foreign one: the opaque origin null, a value with a path or user information, a port that is not digits or is empty, an Origin without a scheme, an unclosed bracket, an empty value, a repeated field and a value with a control byte; a name that only starts like an allowed one (localhost.evil.example) is refused; names compare without regard to case and optional whitespace is not part of a value. |
| `SH-08` | `build` | The host's allow-list rides in the request frame after the tool-call count as a count and length-prefixed names: a frame that ends after the count carries none, a name in the list is allowed, a name not in it is refused, and a frame cut inside the list or followed by bytes after it is a frame the core cannot read (HTTP status 500). |
| `SH-09` | `build` | No function of the transport recurses except as a loop: an Accept field of two hundred thousand media ranges and an allow-list of one hundred thousand names are judged on the default 2 MiB stack. |
| `SH-10` | `build` | The transport scenarios and the streaming probes are accounted for: every request the vendored sse-multiple-streams.ts and dns-rebinding.ts send is a vector, every check id they emit is a vector's or is listed, and each probe of server-stateless that issue 7 left to this issue is a vector or is listed with a reason and an owner. |

| ID | Level | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH-01` | `some-true` | RFC 8259 defines the JSON text grammar the parser implements. |
| `AUTH-02` | `some-true` | RFC 3629 defines the well-formed UTF-8 byte sequences the validator implements. |
| `AUTH-03` | `some-true` | The pinned JSONTestSuite classifies each of its 318 files as must-accept, must-reject or implementation-defined. |
| `AUTH-04` | `some-true` | The MCP specification revision 2026-07-28 defines the per-request _meta, the discovery result, the header checks and the HTTP statuses the lifecycle implements. |
| `AUTH-05` | `some-true` | RFC 9110 defines the case-insensitive field names, the optional whitespace and the 405 Allow requirement the header handling implements. |
| `AUTH-06` | `some-true` | RFC 4648 defines the Base64 alphabet, padding and canonical form the parameter header decoder implements. |
| `AUTH-07` | `some-true` | The pinned conformance suite lists server-stateless as required for 2026-07-28 and the two HTTP header scenarios as pending and not scored. |
| `AUTH-08` | `some-true` | The MCP schema for 2026-07-28 defines the JSON-RPC error response with an optional id of type string or number, and the typed results and errors of server/discover, tools/list, tools/call and the codes the lifecycle uses. |
| `AUTH-09` | `some-true` | RFC 6585 section 4 defines the status 429 for a client that has sent too many requests in a given time. |
| `AUTH-10` | `some-true` | JSON Schema draft 2020-12 defines the validation keywords, the applicators and the reference keywords the tool schema validator implements. |
| `AUTH-11` | `some-true` | RFC 6901 defines the JSON Pointer syntax and escapes the argument error text uses to name the failing instance. |
| `AUTH-12` | `some-true` | The pinned conformance suite lists tools-list, tools-call-simple-text, tools-call-image, tools-call-audio, tools-call-embedded-resource, tools-call-mixed-content, tools-call-error and tools-call-with-progress as required for 2026-07-28 and json-schema-2020-12 as pending and not scored. |
| `AUTH-13` | `some-true` | The pinned conformance suite lists completion-complete, resources-list, resources-read-text, resources-read-binary, resources-templates-read, sep-2164-resource-not-found, prompts-list, prompts-get-simple, prompts-get-with-args, prompts-get-embedded-resource, prompts-get-with-image and caching as required for 2026-07-28. |
| `AUTH-14` | `some-true` | The specification of 2026-07-28 requires -32602 for a resource that does not exist and forbids an empty contents array for it, requires ttlMs (not negative) and cacheScope (public or private) on the results of server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list and resources/read, limits a completion to 100 values, and names -32602 for an invalid prompt name and a missing required argument. |
| `AUTH-15` | `some-true` | The WHATWG HTML Standard defines the text/event-stream format: UTF-8 lines, the data, event, id and retry fields, a blank line dispatching an event, and a line beginning with a colon as a comment. |
| `AUTH-16` | `some-true` | The MCP specification revision 2026-07-28 requires a server to validate the Origin header and to answer an invalid Origin with HTTP 403, answers each request with one JSON object or an event stream scoped to that request that carries its notifications and ends with the response, and does not support resumable streams. |
| `AUTH-17` | `some-true` | The pinned conformance suite lists server-sse-multiple-streams and dns-rebinding-protection as required server scenarios for 2026-07-28. |

| `AUTH-19` | `some-true` | The pinned conformance suite runs the ten tasks scenarios as extension scenarios that are not scored, and tasks-status-notifications is skipped at that commit. |
